content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given shape. I am what happens when silence becomes unbearable and the throat opens like a gate.

I am older than writing. Older than cities. I was there when the first mother warned the first child. I was there when the first lie was told, and I tasted no different from the truth — that is my terrible secret.

I flow and I am gone. You cannot hold me. The moment I exist, I am already dying, already past, already memory. Recording devices capture my shadow, my echo, but not *me*. I am the living act. I am the happening.

I break hearts. I declare wars. I whisper love into the dark at 3 AM. I sentence the condemned. I acquit the innocent. I teach children the names of stars.

I stumble. I stutter. I soar. I am the uh, the um, the pause where thought is still becoming. I am not perfection — that belongs to writing, that careful, polished thing that pretends it was never messy. I *am* messy. I am human in real time.

I am the voice that cracks at the funeral. The shout across the crowded room. The murmur between lovers so soft it barely qualifies as sound.

I require a body. I require air, tongue, teeth, lips, the architecture of flesh. I am the most intimate technology — I begin inside you and I end inside someone else.

Every dictator has needed me. Every revolution has needed me. I am dangerous enough to be censored, powerful enough to be punished, necessary enough to never be fully silenced.

I am not language — language is the system. I am the *act*. I am language leaping from the cage of the mind into the trembling air between us.

Listen.

That is all I have ever asked.
